pageBuilder.text:
What it is like here

There are five of us, in a converted byre with a trial garden outside the door. Everyone who designs a garden also visits it, measures it and, often, plants it. We work four long days in the studio and one on site, and we try hard not to work weekends.

Who we look for

  • People who know plants, or are determined to.
  • People who listen well, and draw clearly.
  • People who are happy in wellies in February.

pageBuilder.caption: Some of our favourite work is with schools and community groups.

pageBuilder.quote: I came for the planting. I stayed because everyone here still gets excited about a good hedge.

Open roles

pageBuilder.heading: How we work
pageBuilder.subheading: Slowly at the start, so the garden can look after itself at the end.

pageBuilder.text:
We start with the ground

Every project begins with a visit and a soil pit. We look at what grows already, where the sun falls, where water collects, and how you use the space now. We ask a lot of questions, and we write down the answers.

We draw by hand first

Our first ideas are always sketches, on paper, at your kitchen table if you'll let us. It keeps the conversation open. Once the layout is agreed, we draw it properly and plan the planting in detail.

We plant for the place

We choose plants that will be happy in your soil and your weather, so they need less watering, feeding and fussing. Most of our planting is perennial, much of it native or wildlife-friendly, and all of it chosen to look good for as much of the year as possible.

pageBuilder.caption: Planting that suits its place needs far less looking after.

pageBuilder.quote: We have never regretted digging a pit. We have regretted not digging one.

pageBuilder.text:
We come back

We visit every garden we design at least once a year for the first three years. We see what has thrived and what has sulked, and we help you adjust. Gardens change, and the design should be allowed to change with them.

pageBuilder.heading: Would this suit your garden?
pageBuilder.ctaText: Tell us about your space and we will suggest where to begin.

pageBuilder.heading: What we do
pageBuilder.subheading: From a single border to a whole school grounds, we can help at whatever stage you are at.

pageBuilder.text:
Garden design

A full design for your garden, from the first visit and soil pit to a planting plan and drawings a contractor can build from. Most of our residential projects take three to four months from first visit to finished drawings.

Planting design

If the layout of your garden works but the planting doesn't, we can design the borders on their own. We'll give you a plan, a plant list and, if you'd like, come and lay the plants out on the day.

Consultations

A two-hour visit where we walk your garden with you, answer your questions and send you a short written report afterwards. A good place to start if you're not sure what you need.

Schools and community spaces

We design with the people who will use the space, not just for them. We keep some time each year for projects with small budgets.

pageBuilder.caption: A long border, three years after planting.

pageBuilder.quote: We only wanted advice about one border. Two hours later we had a plan for the whole garden and the confidence to do it ourselves.

pageBuilder.text:
What it costs

Every garden is different, so we quote for each one after a first visit. As a guide, a consultation costs £240, and most full garden designs fall between £2,500 and £6,000. We'll always tell you the fee before we start, and it won't change unless the brief does.

pageBuilder.ctaText: Book a consultation. It is the easiest way to find out what your garden needs.

pageBuilder.subheading: We design gardens and outdoor spaces across the north of England, and we come back to see how they grow.

pageBuilder.text:
Who we are

Northfold is a landscape architecture and garden design studio based near Corbridge in Northumberland. There are five of us. Ellie founded the studio in 2016, and between us we have trained as landscape architects, horticulturists, nursery growers and, in one case, a geography teacher.

We work on private gardens, schools, community spaces and the occasional public project, mostly within a couple of hours of the studio. That is deliberate. We like to know the soil and the weather where we work, and to be close enough to call in.

pageBuilder.caption: The studio, in a converted byre near Corbridge.

pageBuilder.quote: They listened more than they talked, which is rare. The garden feels like ours, not like theirs.

pageBuilder.text:
What we believe

  • The best gardens are the ones people use.
  • Plants should suit the place they are planted, not the other way round.
  • A healthy garden should rarely be ripped out to make way for a fashionable one.
  • A designer should still turn up five years later to see how it's going.

pageBuilder.heading: Have a garden in mind?
pageBuilder.ctaText: Tell us a little about it. We reply to everyone within a few days.

pageBuilder.heading: Get in touch
pageBuilder.subheading: Tell us a little about your garden or project, and we will reply within a few days.

pageBuilder.text:
The studio

Northfold, The Byre, Dilston Lane, Corbridge, Northumberland NE45 5XX

We are in the studio Monday to Thursday, and usually on site on Fridays. Visits are by appointment, but the kettle is always on.

What to tell us

  • Where the garden is, roughly how big, and which way it faces.
  • What you would like to change, and what you love and want to keep.
  • Any timing you have in mind, and a rough budget if you know it.

Photos are always welcome.

pageBuilder.caption: The bench from our show garden, now outside the studio door.

pageBuilder.quote: The first conversation was so easy. No pressure, just good questions and a lot of enthusiasm.

pageBuilder.heading: Prefer to talk?
pageBuilder.ctaText: Call the studio on 01434 000 000, Monday to Thursday, 9 to 5.

pageBuilder.text:
## We start with the ground

Every project begins with a visit and a soil pit. We look at what grows already, where the sun falls, where water collects, and how you use the space now. We ask a lot of questions, and we write down the answers.

## We draw by hand first

Our first ideas are always sketches, on paper, at your kitchen table if you'll let us. It keeps the conversation open. Once the layout is agreed, we draw it properly and plan the planting in detail.

## We plant for the place

We choose plants that will be happy in your soil and your weather, so they need less watering, feeding and fussing. Most of our planting is perennial, much of it native or wildlife-friendly, and all of it chosen to look good for as much of the year as possible.

pageBuilder.caption: Planting that suits its place needs far less looking after.

pageBuilder.quote: We have never regretted digging a pit. We have regretted not digging one.

pageBuilder.text:
## We come back

We visit every garden we design at least once a year for the first three years. We see what has thrived and what has sulked, and we help you adjust. Gardens change, and the design should be allowed to change with them.

pageBuilder.heading: Would this suit your garden?
pageBuilder.ctaText: Tell us about your space and we will suggest where to begin.

pageBuilder.heading: Working at Northfold
pageBuilder.subheading: We are a small team, and we grow slowly. When we do look for someone, this is where we say so.

pageBuilder.text:
What it is like here

There are five of us, in a converted byre with a trial garden outside the door. Everyone who designs a garden also visits it, measures it and, often, plants it. We work four long days in the studio and one on site, and we try hard not to work weekends.

Who we look for

  • People who know plants, or are determined to.
  • People who listen well, and draw clearly.
  • People who are happy in wellies in February.

pageBuilder.caption: Some of our favourite work is with schools and community groups.

pageBuilder.quote: I came for the planting. I stayed because everyone here still gets excited about a good hedge.

We are not hiring right now. We are always glad to hear from students looking for a placement, and from designers and horticulturists who would like to work with us in future. Send a short note and a few pages of work, and we will keep it on file.

pageBuilder.text:
## Garden design

A full design for your garden, from the first visit and soil pit to a planting plan and drawings a contractor can build from. Most of our residential projects take three to four months from first visit to finished drawings.

## Planting design

If the layout of your garden works but the planting doesn't, we can design the borders on their own. We'll give you a plan, a plant list and, if you'd like, come and lay the plants out on the day.

## Consultations

A two-hour visit where we walk your garden with you, answer your questions and send you a short written report afterwards. A good place to start if you're not sure what you need.

## Schools and community spaces

We design with the people who will use the space, not just for them. We keep some time each year for projects with small budgets.

pageBuilder.caption: A long border, three years after planting.

pageBuilder.quote: We only wanted advice about one border. Two hours later we had a plan for the whole garden and the confidence to do it ourselves.

pageBuilder.text:
## What it costs

Every garden is different, so we quote for each one after a first visit. As a guide, a consultation costs £240, and most full garden designs fall between £2,500 and £6,000. We'll always tell you the fee before we start, and it won't change unless the brief does.

pageBuilder.ctaText: Book a consultation. It is the easiest way to find out what your garden needs.

## Who we are

Northfold is a landscape architecture and garden design studio based near Corbridge in Northumberland. There are five of us. Ellie founded the studio in 2016, and between us we have trained as landscape architects, horticulturists, nursery growers and, in one case, a geography teacher.

We work on private gardens, schools, community spaces and the occasional public project, mostly within a couple of hours of the studio. That is deliberate. We like to know the soil and the weather where we work, and to be close enough to call in.

pageBuilder.caption: The studio, in a converted byre near Corbridge.

pageBuilder.quote: They listened more than they talked, which is rare. The garden feels like ours, not like theirs.

pageBuilder.text:
## What we believe

- The best gardens are the ones people use.
- Plants should suit the place they are planted, not the other way round.
- A healthy garden should rarely be ripped out to make way for a fashionable one.
- A designer should still turn up five years later to see how it's going.

pageBuilder.ctaText: Tell us a little about it. We reply to everyone within a few days.

pageBuilder.heading: Working at Northfold
pageBuilder.subheading: We are a small team, and we grow slowly. When we do look for someone, this is where we say so.

pageBuilder.text:
## What it is like here

There are five of us, in a converted byre with a trial garden outside the door. Everyone who designs a garden also visits it, measures it and, often, plants it. We work four long days in the studio and one on site, and we try hard not to work weekends.

## Who we look for

- People who know plants, or are determined to.
- People who listen well, and draw clearly.
- People who are happy in wellies in February.

pageBuilder.caption: Some of our favourite work is with schools and community groups.

pageBuilder.quote: I came for the planting. I stayed because everyone here still gets excited about a good hedge.

pageBuilder.text:
## Open roles

We are not hiring right now. We are always glad to hear from students looking for a placement, and from designers and horticulturists who would like to work with us in future. Send a short note and a few pages of work, and we will keep it on file.

pageBuilder.heading: How we work
pageBuilder.subheading: Slowly at the start, so the garden can look after itself at the end.

pageBuilder.text:
## We start with the ground

Every project begins with a visit and a soil pit. We look at what grows already, where the sun falls, where water collects, and how you use the space now. We ask a lot of questions, and we write down the answers.

## We draw by hand first

Our first ideas are always sketches, on paper, at your kitchen table if you'll let us. It keeps the conversation open. Once the layout is agreed, we draw it properly and plan the planting in detail.

## We plant for the place

We choose plants that will be happy in your soil and your weather, so they need less watering, feeding and fussing. Most of our planting is perennial, much of it native or wildlife-friendly, and all of it chosen to look good for as much of the year as possible.

pageBuilder.caption: Planting that suits its place needs far less looking after.

pageBuilder.quote: We have never regretted digging a pit. We have regretted not digging one.

pageBuilder.text:
## We come back

We visit every garden we design at least once a year for the first three years. We see what has thrived and what has sulked, and we help you adjust. Gardens change, and the design should be allowed to change with them.
